findings.title: Paired-device review gate is defeated by content padded past the 600-byte preview
findings.scenario: A paired device writes a 2 KB .txt note through an ordinary remote filesystem.write (inert extension, allowed). The first ~600 bytes are benign filler; a payload (require('fs').writeFileSync('ran.flag',...)) sits after byte 600. A workstation Mission then runs terminal.exec 'node notes.txt'. The Host asks for review: pendingRemoteReview()/describeRemoteChange() show only size, a 16-hex SHA-256 prefix and bytes.subarray(0,600) of the file, with the prompt text 'Review their content before allowing'. The payload is not shown. The workstation allows once; the answer acknowledges the change record (acknowledgeRemoteChanges), not the bytes that were shown, so the whole file is run and the payload executes. Probe confirmed: the prompt did not contain 'payload-ran', nothing ran before approval, and after allow_once the mission completed with ran.flag created.
findings.evidence: Probe (copy of remote-authority.test.ts, absolute imports, throwaway folder, since deleted): 'R9A bytes= 2157 PROMPT=... content: "// benign header line ... be…"', then 'R9A final mission state= completed ran.flag exists= true'. Related code: manager.server.ts:74-85 (describeRemoteChange, 600-byte preview), 2316-2326 (pendingRemoteReview lists only that preview), 3646-3648 (allow_once acks request.remoteReview ids). Existing test R41 only covers files small enough to show whole.
findings.recommendation: Do not treat the 600-byte preview as a review of the file. Either refuse to run code over any reviewed file larger than the preview (or whose full content cannot be shown), or show the full content (bounded by a hard cap that fails closed above it) and state truncation explicitly. Bind the acknowledgement to the SHA-256 of the full file, and have the exec/session launch re-check that hash against the acknowledged value so content the workstation did not see cannot run. Add a regression where the payload sits past byte 600.

findings.title: Device-started workstation Mission writes are not attributed, so mid-run hold and review miss them
findings.scenario: A workstation-approved Mission whose plan has no shell, terminal, Git-mutation or EXECUTE steps (only filesystem.write) passes deviceStartRefusal, so a paired device can call mission.start on it. Mission start records no actor (MissionManager.start(mission) at manager.server.ts:856 and commands.server.ts:60-61 do not pass access.actor). remoteActorFor() then returns null: the envelope is trusted (grantedBy 'workstation') and the step has no device-answered approvedOnce. So remoteMutationHeld() in bus.server.ts:165 never holds the write and remoteMutationStarted() (bus.server.ts:307) never records it into remote_changes. Probe: a workstation terminal run was live (bus.liveCode.size===1), the device started the write Mission, and the write landed mid-run (ran.txt='phone', not the 'host' content the live run had started with), with pendingRemoteChanges()=0. Control: the same write answered by the device after a device approval was held ('code approved on the Windows Host is running (terminal.exec)'), so the gap is specifically the device-start path. The written content is plan-fixed, so the impact is the device choosing the timing of a workstation-approved overwrite under live code, which breaks the stated mid-run hold invariant.
findings.evidence: Probe R9-PROBE-B: 'R9B editState= completed writes= [ 'filesystem.write:succeeded' ] pendingRemoteChanges= 0 ran.txt= phone'. Code: manager.server.ts:2303-2311 (remoteActorFor), 2340-2350 (remoteMutationHeld returns null with no actor), commands.server.ts:60 (deviceStartRefusal allows pure-write plans), manager.server.ts:856-867 (start with no actor), bus.server.ts:165 and :307.
findings.recommendation: Record the actor that started each Mission (and each start/resume) in the Mission record and treat a device-started Mission's mutations as device-attributable. Alternatively, have deviceStartRefusal refuse to start while any workstation code is live (liveCodeExecutions() non-empty), and re-check at each mutation. Add a regression for device mission.start during a live workstation run.

findings.title: One-time workstation approval exempts all later same-action device writes on that step from the mid-run hold
findings.scenario: remoteMutationHeld() returns null whenever the step's approvedOnce action equals the request action and it was resolved by the workstation. It never compares path, params or digest. For a remote-envelope skill step, the workstation's one-time answer for one filesystem.write therefore lets every later device-attributable filesystem.write on that step through while workstation-approved code is live. Capability steps run one action, so the exposure is limited to multi-write skill steps. Confirmed by a fake-object probe that calls the real remoteActorFor/remoteMutationHeld: approvedOnce resolved by 'workstation' for a.txt, then a device write to other.txt with live code returns null (not held). Skill one-time scope ('matching action within approved roots') is already broad by design, so this mainly extends the hold exemption to the same breadth.
findings.evidence: Probe output: 'approved-once path a.txt, device write other.txt -> null' and 'C2 CONFIRMED'. Code: manager.server.ts:2343-2346. The skill one-time scope is in bus.server.ts:175 (oneTime from oneTimeAction).
findings.recommendation: Bind the exemption to the exact operation: compare the approved request's operation/params digest (as capabilityOperation or agenticFingerprint do) with this request, or exempt only the single admitted execution by consuming the one-time allowance on first use.

findings.title: Mid-run hold ignores provider change: survivors of a shell attempt stop holding device changes after a reroute to a tool-free provider
findings.scenario: A Mission child runs as codex (or claude write), its root process exits, and a descendant (e.g. a dev server started by the session) survives, so watchSurvivors records it under key '<taskId>#n'. The completion loop then reroutes the same task record to ollama (tool-free) via startSession (bunny-host/manager.server.ts ~1288). liveCodeExecutions() classifies every lingering entry by the task's CURRENT provider (db.get(id).provider), so the codex survivor is judged tool_free and dropped. remoteMutationHeld() therefore returns null and a paired-device filesystem.write lands while the workstation-approved survivor is still running. Probed: with the record fabricated as codex, liveCodeExecutions() returns ['codex session task-1'] and remoteMutationHeld(device write) returns the hold message; with the record fabricated as ollama, liveCodeExecutions() returns [] and remoteMutationHeld returns null.
findings.evidence: Probe (throwaway, mkdtemp under OS temp, since deleted): tasks.lingering.set('task-1#1', [{pid:4242,ppid:1,createdAt:1}]); tasks.db.get monkeypatched to return {provider:'codex'|'ollama', mission:{...}, executionScope:{access:'write'}} for task-1. Outputs: codex -> ["codex session task-1"]; ollama -> []; remoteMutationHeld(device filesystem.write) codex -> held, ollama -> null. Key creation: bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1706-1709 (watchSurvivors, key = `${id}#${++survivorWatches}`, no provider or access stored). Classification: bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:2328-2336. Note: the record was fabricated to reach the classification path; the reroute itself was not driven end-to-end.
findings.recommendation: Store the attempt's provider and access on the lingering entry at watchSurvivors time (for example lingering value {provider, access, alive}) and classify survivors by that snapshot, not by the current task record. Add a regression test: codex write attempt leaves a survivor, the task is rerouted to ollama, and a device filesystem.write is still held until the survivor ends.

findings.title: Superseded desktop re-ask is recorded as a user denial, contrary to its own comment
findings.scenario: When a workstation allow_once is made stale by a project change (DesktopRequestStale), respond() saves the original request with resolution 'deny' and resolvedBy '<actor> (superseded: project changed)', then re-asks. The comment on the same block says it is 'never as a user denial'. The audit timeline, inbox and any consumer of request.resolution therefore see a denial. Authority is not widened (no grant is minted and the step stays waiting), so this is a record-accuracy defect only.
findings.evidence: bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:3631: this.store.saveRequest({ ...request, resolvedAt: Date.now(), resolution: "deny", resolvedBy: `${by} (superseded: project changed)` }); the comment in the same catch block says 'Superseded, never as a user denial'.
findings.recommendation: Mark superseded requests with a distinct resolution (for example 'superseded') or leave them open and close them through the inbox, and make the audit event say superseded, not denied.

findings.title: Device-triggered Agent writes under workstation consent are not attributed or reviewed
findings.scenario: A paired device may resume a workstation-consented Agent whose permitted capabilities contain filesystem.write but no EXECUTE or terminal capability (deviceResumeRefusal passes). The model's filesystem.write calls then run under the workstation envelope with no one-time answer, so remoteActorFor() returns null, bus.request does not call remoteMutationStarted, and no pendingRemoteChanges row is created. The Host-wide review gate therefore does not list these files before a later workstation-approved code run loads them. This may be within the workstation's own consent, so it is recorded here as a design observation rather than a violation.
findings.evidence: remoteActorFor at bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:2303-2312 returns null unless the envelope is remote or step.approvedOnce was answered by a device; bus.server.ts:307 records only when remoteActorFor is non-null.
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly whether device-triggered resumes count as paired-device authority for review purposes; if yes, record writes made during a device-initiated resume as remote changes.

findings.title: Revoked device's one-time approvals survive workstation revocation
findings.scenario: A paired device answers allow_once on a workstation-envelope ask (or a planned in-envelope write). The step keeps approvedOnce {requestId, action} with request.resolvedBy = device:<id> until it runs. The workstation then revokes that device. endDeviceGrants (http.server.ts ~822-870) ends only device-created approval batches, device-approved Agentic consents and device-granted Mission envelopes. It never clears a step's approvedOnce, so the one-time allowance still executes (bus.request -> decide oneTime). The window is open while the step is queued or while the Agent is paused (device agent.pause is allowed and respond refuses while PAUSED), and it closes when the workstation resumes the Agent. Restart does clear it for ready/running steps.
findings.evidence: http.server.ts:732 calls endDeviceGrants only when local; endDeviceGrants (822-870) has no approvedOnce handling. approvedOnce is set at manager.server.ts:3738 and :3764 from the answering request. decide() (authorization.server.ts oneTime branch) checks no device-revocation state. Code-read only; not probed end-to-end.
findings.recommendation: On workstation revocation of a device, clear approvedOnce on every non-completed step whose answering request.resolvedBy equals device:<id>, and fail that step closed. Add a test: device answers, device is revoked, step later runs -> refused.

findings.title: GitHub READ actions run gh outside the Host-wide review gate
findings.scenario: github.pr_list, github.issue_list and github.repo_view are READ risk and spawn gh in the mission folder. runsCode() returns false for them (it covers only terminal.exec, GIT_MUTATIONS and non-Calculator EXECUTE). The bus review gate (bus.server.ts:169) also tests only runsCode(...) || action.startsWith('git.'), so these run while paired-device changes are unacknowledged. remoteExecutionRefusal() returns null for READ, so a remote envelope may run them with no desktop step. Practical exposure is small: gh children are job-object owned and hardened under remote authority, and device writes cannot create .git config, .gitattributes or executables. It still breaks the stated invariant that no non-direct Bunny program run starts while a device change is unreviewed.
findings.evidence: Probe: runsCode('github.pr_list',{cwd:'.'},'READ') = false; remoteExecutionRefusal(...) = null. Manifests at connectors.server.ts:18-20 (risk READ). Owned gh run at connectors.server.ts:46.
findings.recommendation: Treat any action whose adapter spawns a program as code-running for the review gate and the mid-run hold: add the github.* actions to runsCode (or a PROGRAM_ACTIONS set) and extend the review and liveCode tests to cover them.

findings.title: Review prompt shows only the first 600 bytes of each changed file
findings.scenario: describeRemoteChange() shows size, a 16-hex SHA-256 prefix and only bytes 0-599 as preview. Content past byte 600 is never shown, and the SHA prefix cannot be checked by a human. A device-approved remote Mission can have a planned filesystem.write whose content is larger than 600 bytes, with a payload past the preview. The workstation allow_once then authorizes a code run over that file (the review is the authoritative control). Preconditions: a planned or later-run command must execute that file (the device chooses only among planned operations). This is a truncation limit of the stated design; the owner should decide whether files above the preview size need full display or an explicit override. The preview also leaves LRM/RLM (U+200E/U+200F) unsanitized, so bidi spoofing is possible in the preview text. The function also reads each shown file in full, synchronously, on every gate evaluation.
findings.evidence: manager.server.ts:80 `bytes.subarray(0, 600)`; sanitizer regex at line 80 omits ‎-‏; describeRemoteChange reads readFileSync(path) for up to REVIEW_PAGE=12 paths per pendingRemoteReview() call.
findings.recommendation: Refuse allow_once (or require an explicit 'content not fully shown' acknowledgement) when size > preview length. Show the full content up to a larger cap, add U+200E/U+200F to the sanitizer, and cache hashes by (path, mtime, size) to avoid full-file reads on every gate check.

findings.title: Denylist misses inert-extension execution configs (INFO, by design)
findings.scenario: Probed under remote authority (filesystem.write): docker-compose.override.yml, compose.override.yaml, .nycrc.json and x.cjs.txt are ALLOW. nyc, docker compose and the Node CJS loader can execute such files. The denylist covers (docker-)?compose.yml only, and the agent-config dir list omits .opencode, .zed, .agent(s), .amazonq and .trae. Bunny-run tools are still covered by the Host-wide review gate on terminal, Git and shell sessions, so this is an external-tool gap the owner already accepted as a denylist-by-design limitation.
findings.evidence: Probe on the throwaway project: remoteExecutionRefusal('filesystem.write',{path:'docker-compose.override.yml'},'WRITE',root) = null; same for .nycrc.json and x.cjs.txt. EXECUTION_CONFIG_FILE/EXECUTION_CONFIG_DIR at authorization.server.ts:502-503.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add compose.override.ya?ml, docker-compose.override.ya?ml and .nycrc* to the denylist and extend the dir list. Otherwise document these as accepted external-tool gaps.

findings.title: Paired device sees another Mission's paired-device change paths and content previews in ask reasons
findings.scenario: A paired device (device A) approves a Mission whose remote envelope writes secret-a.txt with content SECRET-A-CONTENT, so the change is recorded in remote_changes. Later a different Mission B (or a different paired device B) raises a git.status or other code-running ask. pendingRemoteReview() is Host-wide (manager.server.ts:2316, no mission filter; store.server.ts:158 pendingRemoteChanges has no mission filter), so the review listing for Mission A's file, including its SHA-256 prefix and up to 600 characters of content, is written into Mission B's request.reason at bus.server.ts:171. Host HTTP viewFor applies remoteVerdicts to every principal (http.server.ts:338) and remoteVerdicts keeps the reason field (manager.server.ts:2148 onward, spread of the request), so the device projection carries the listing. A device therefore reads paths and content of files written under another Mission's envelope, including roots that device may not otherwise read. Confidentiality only; it does not authorize any execution, and the workstation prompt is correct.
findings.evidence: Probe (throwaway mkdtemp folder, repo modules by file URL, deleted afterwards): Mission A approved by device:probe-phone wrote secret-a.txt; file on disk = SECRET-A-CONTENT. Mission B (workstation, capability git.status) produced ask action=git.status desktopRequired=true. mission.get as device:probe-phone returned the ask with reason containing 'secret-a.txt' = true and 'SECRET-A-CONTENT' = true. Review listing built at manager.server.ts:2324 (describeRemoteChange, 600-char preview). Note: the probe used the same owner's paired device for both missions; cross-device visibility follows from the Host-wide query.
findings.recommendation: Keep the full review listing for the workstation prompt only. For device projections (remoteVerdicts / viewFor / mission.get), strip or redact review listing text from reason (e.g. replace the listing with a count and a note that the workstation reviews it), or scope pendingRemoteReview's listing to changes made by the viewing device's own missions and roots. Consider also dropping the content preview from any text that reaches a device.

Lens results (no concrete device escalation found):
- Device allow_once (deviceRequestRefusal candidate loop): judged on executor params plus every same-action verification check, file_exists mapped to filesystem.read/exists, remoteExecutionRefusal and scopeViolation applied for every device answer regardless of envelope. Cross-app inputs (crossAppInputs) only inject `content` for filesystem.write, which is not an execution parameter, so the judged path/command/target is the executed one.
- approvedOnce: device answers never set the path-root extension (capabilityRequest `once` requires trusted-local resolvedBy). Remote decide() checks remoteExecutionRefusal before oneTime, so a device one-time cannot pass a refused action. Retry clears approvedOnce on non-completed steps; restart clears it for failed missions and ready/running/verifying steps; blocked steps are only revived by Retry (which clears them).
- allow_batch: batches are computer-family only, consultBatch requires a planned-step stepId plus exact operation digest, remote envelopes return before rescue when remoteExecutionRefusal applies, agentic rescue requires workstation-created batches. Calculator-only batches still work for consented cross-app Agents and non-Agent Missions.
- provider.execute: device answers require deviceResumeRefusal, deviceMayLaunch and taskViolation null; reroute under a device-approved task is blocked by the deviceApproved marker and by deviceStartRefusal shell candidates; remote shell launches are refused in missionScopeCheck (check and launch) and tasks.launch/reroute call both phases.
- project.context: device answer possible only for model steps; it sets approvedOnce for an action no step executes and the CONTEXT_CHANGED throw recurs on relaunch, so no bypass (INFO-level observation at most, not reported).
- Agent consent: re-consent refuses EXECUTE/terminal/git manifests; filesystem write/delete judged per path at execution; cross_app computer ops are digest-bound to reviewed operations.
- Stale/superseded: DesktopRequestStale re-asks and records resolvedBy "workstation (superseded...)" which fails isTrustedLocalActor; mutationSequence is a synchronous row count so a device write cannot land between ask and answer for filesystem.write (write + remote_change record occur in the same synchronous adapter call; browser.download and git mutations are refused for devices).
- Probes (throwaway folder under OS temp, removed afterwards; no repo files written): inertDataPath/executionConfigPath/remoteExecutionRefusal on ~20 names (package.json, package.json., tsconfig.base.json, node_modules, .github, a.ps1, x.txt:s, x.lnk/.url/.hta/.jse, notes.md, A.MD, trailing-dot/space), providerSessionAuthority per provider/access, isRemoteEnvelope for legacy JSON and mislabelled envelopes, Calculator title/pid/open_app/target variants, git.diff READ, browser.download. All results matched the intended policy.
- Permitted test run: `node --experimental-strip-types --test src/lib/bunny-missions/remote-authority.test.ts` = 61 pass, 0 fail. test-results/ unchanged (git status clean for that path).

Accepted/out-of-scope notes (not reported): 600-character preview is the documented review basis; denylist gaps such as opencode.json or .goreleaser.yml are covered by the Host-wide review gate for any Bunny-run code; direct workstation runs, Git-read filter drivers and owner-started tools are listed limitations. Survivor tracking (C) and the denylist (B) were checked only as far as they affect device answers.

result.reasoning:
Verified by static reading; I did not run a probe or the test command, and I did not modify any repo file.

The mechanism is real:
- bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1706-1709 (watchSurvivors) stores only `lingering.set("<taskId>#<n>", ...)`. The entry records no provider or access.
- bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:2328-2336 (liveCodeExecutions) classifies every lingering key by `this.tasks.db.get(id)`, i.e. the task record's CURRENT provider, at call time.
- bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1296-1316 (retry/reroute inside the completion loop) updates the same task record's provider/model via `this.update(current, {provider: target.provider, ...})`. So after a codex attempt's root exits and its descendant survives, the loop calls watchSurvivors (around line 1425, with the codex-era record), then reroutes the same record to ollama. The survivor entry is then judged tool_free by providerSessionAuthority("ollama", "write") and dropped.
- Reroute to ollama is admitted for a Mission: admitAgenticProvider and missionScopeCheck do not block it on that basis, and the task's executionScope.access stays "write".
- remoteMutationHeld (manager.server.ts:2340-2350) therefore returns null while the workstation-approved codex-spawned process is still alive, and a paired-device filesystem.write is allowed.

The existing tests do not cover this. remote-authority.test.ts:1245-1331 (F01-R40 and related) checks lingering entries and their pids only, with no reroute and no classification after a provider change.

I did not find a precondition that prevents it. The lineage is tracked, so the survivor is not one of the accepted "never observed" limitations. The restart note does not apply, since the process survives within the same Host run.

Severity stays MEDIUM rather than HIGH. The paired device can write only inert data types (round-7 allowlist), and the surviving process must itself be a workstation-approved process that consumes those files in a code-executing way, such as a watcher or an MDX-style dev server. That is an invariant gap in the mid-run hold rather than a direct device-to-code path.

Could not refute. Code path confirmed by reading and by a throwaway probe in an mkdtemp folder under the OS temp dir (deleted afterwards).

Confirmed:
- src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:2333 classifies every lingering survivor by the CURRENT task record: `task.provider === "ollama" && !task.mission ? "tool_free" : providerSessionAuthority(task.provider, ...)`. No provider or access is stored on the lingering entry.
- src/lib/bunny-host/manager.server.ts:1706-1709 (watchSurvivors) keys entries `${id}#${n}` and stores only the process list, so the attempt's provider is lost.
- Probe: calling MissionManager.prototype.liveCodeExecutions with a fake `this` holding lingering `task-1#1` and a task record with access write returned ["codex session task-1"] for provider codex, [] for ollama, and ["claude session task-1"] for claude. The survivor is therefore dropped once the record is rerouted to ollama.
- The reroute path exists: the completion loop calls watchSurvivors after each attempt (line ~1426), then on failure calls rerouteFromDecision and startSession, which mutates the same task record's provider (host manager ~1300-1325). Nothing in startSession, rerouteFromDecision or the loop checks lingering survivors or stops them.
- For a non-agentic Mission child, the reroute admission (providerScopeViolation -> remoteSessionViolation) allows ollama, since tool_free is inside REMOTE_SESSION_CEILING. Ollama write-scope children are not blocked by the scope checks.
- The survivor's watch keeps running (check() reschedules while alive.size > 0), so the workstation-approved process really is still live during the bypass window.
- bus.server.ts:165 holds only when remoteMutationHeld returns a message, so a device filesystem.write in that window lands.

Not refuted, because none of the listed dispositions or accepted limitations cover it. Bunny itself started and observed the survivor, so it is not an unobserved external tool. The impact is bounded: the device write must be a permitted data-type file, and something in the still-running survivor must consume it. The impact is therefore MEDIUM rather than higher.

Not driven end-to-end: the full codex-fail -> survivor -> reroute -> device write sequence was not run. The reroute precondition (a failed attempt whose failure taxonomy permits reroute, and ollama in the recorded fallback order) was reasoned from code, not executed. No repo files were changed and no repo tests were run.

Not refuted. The gap is real at code level, though the practical reach is narrower than the finding states.

Confirmed by code read (no probe run; no repo files touched; no test-results change):
- http.server.ts:720-740 calls endDeviceGrants only when `local` (workstation). endDeviceGrants (822-873) handles device-created batches, device-approved Agentic authorizations, and device-granted Mission envelopes (`envelope.grantedBy !== deviceActor` -> continue). A workstation-granted envelope is untouched, and no `approvedOnce` handling exists anywhere in http.server.ts (grep confirmed).
- A device answer sets `approvedOnce: {requestId, action}` at manager.server.ts:3738/3764, and the answering request keeps `resolvedBy = device:<id>`.
- The one-time path is not actor-gated. manager.server.ts:1537 sets `oneTimeAction` from `step.approvedOnce.action` regardless of who answered; only the root widening at 1524 checks isTrustedLocalActor. bus.server.ts:175 passes `oneTime` to decide(). decide() (authorization.server.ts:365-374) checks only `envelope.revokedAt` (371) and the expiry, then returns allow on `context.oneTime`. The revoked-device state is never read by the missions layer: the only `revoked_at` reads are in device-authority, manager.server.ts:344 (listing) and http.server.ts. So a stale device one-time allowance executes once its step is admitted.
- Clearing paths exist for Retry (manager.server.ts ~3908/3917) and Host restart (~4161, ~4203-4222), but none runs on device revocation.

Narrowing the scenario:
- The finding's closing claim is inverted. The window does not close when the workstation resumes the Agent. Resume is what lets the stale step run. The window closes only on Retry, restart, or completion.
- A device cannot answer while the Agent is paused (respond refuses PAUSED, manager.server.ts ~3585-3587). The step is admitted via schedule() -> setImmediate (manager.server.ts 870-885) and the admission gate (agent-runtime.server.ts 74-78). So the realistic path is: device answers, device issues agent.pause before admission (a narrow race), workstation revokes the device, workstation later resumes. Any tick overlap that defers admission widens the window somewhat.
- Impact is bounded to the exact planned, in-envelope, non-sensitive filesystem step the device approved (or a Calculator op / tool-free launch). No code execution and no scope expansion results. This matches the stated intent gap ("A lost device's authority ends with it", http.server.ts:730), not an owner-policy violation.

Severity LOW is appropriate. The recommended fix (clear approvedOnce on non-completed steps whose answering request.resolvedBy is device:<id> during revocation, and add a device-answer / revoke / pause / resume test) is sound.

The core fact is true: at src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:3631 the superseded request is saved with resolution "deny" (resolvedBy "<actor> (superseded: project changed)"), while the comment at the same block says "never as a user denial". No grant is minted (desktopGrant is only set when mintDesktopGrant succeeds, and the catch throws), the step is re-asked through askPermission, and the old record is never referenced by step.pendingRequestId, approvedOnce, or any authority check. Authority is not widened, so this is not a security issue.

The claimed impact is overstated. (1) The catch block emits no audit event, so the audit timeline gets no denial from this path. (2) The only code reader of request.resolution is src/lib/bunny-host/presentation.ts:374, and it looks up the request via step.pendingRequestId (line 359). The superseded request is no longer that pointer, and the "Denied" label only applies to failed steps, which this step is not. (3) The inbox is resolved by requestId, not by resolution. No UI under src/components reads resolution. The effect is limited to the raw stored record field being inconsistent with the comment and with its resolvedBy text. The existing test at src/lib/bunny-missions/remote-authority.test.ts:894 asserts only resolvedBy matches /superseded/ and desktopGrant is undefined. I did not run the test or any probe. Filing as INFO record-accuracy nit, not LOW.

Not refuted. The claim holds on code read and in a throwaway probe.

Code path (verified):
- http.server.ts:726-732 (device.revoke) sets devices.revoked_at, closes streams and calls endDeviceGrants only for a workstation revoke.
- endDeviceGrants (http.server.ts:822-870) touches only approval_batches created by the device, agentic_authorizations approved by the device, and mission envelopes with grantedBy === device. It never reads or clears step.approvedOnce, and it never touches a workstation-granted envelope.
- manager.server.ts:3738 and :3764 set approvedOnce from the answering request. Nothing checks the answering actor's device status afterwards.
- bus.server.ts:175 passes oneTime when oneTimeAction matches. authorization.server.ts:374 returns allow for oneTime. No branch in decide() reads device revocation state. grep finds no missions-side reader of devices.revoked_at.
- manager.server.ts:1523-1537 widens roots only for a workstation answer, so a device one-time allowance stays inside projectRoots.
- Retry (manager ~3908) and Host restart (~4203) do clear approvedOnce. Nothing else does.

Probe (throwaway temp dir, deleted afterwards): a workstation-approved Mission with a filesystem.write step was given approvedOnce from a request resolved by device:phone. A devices row was then marked revoked_at, mirroring the workstation revoke. Mission scheduling then ran the step: a.txt was written with the planned content, the step completed, and approvedOnce was cleared. The repo's git status is unchanged (27 entries). No repo tests were run.

Realistic window: normally a ready step runs on the next tick, so the window needs the step to be held. The device can pause its own Agent, which holds admission (manager ~1000 missionPauseGate) while the step stays ready with approvedOnce. The window then closes on workstation resume, Retry or restart. This is a bounded, exact, in-envelope, non-sensitive filesystem write that the device approved before revocation. It does not give code execution, shell, or action outside the planned step or Mission envelope. The owner's dispositions do not list one-time allowances surviving device revocation, so it is not covered by them. Severity stays LOW, consistent with the reporter's rating.

The defect is real but record-accuracy only. Verified in src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts: respond() catch block at lines 3627-3634 calls this.store.saveRequest({...request, resolution: "deny", resolvedBy: `${by} (superseded: project changed)`}), directly above the comment "Superseded, never as a user denial". The request therefore carries resolution "deny". Authority is not widened: no desktopGrant is minted (mintDesktopGrant throws before any grant), approvedOnce is never set to this request, and the step is re-pointed to a fresh request by askPermission (lines 3457-3478, setStep to waiting_for_approval with the new pendingRequestId). The authorization gates that read resolution (lines 2648, 2711) only accept allow_once on approvedOnce requests, and the superseded record can never be approvedOnce. The test at remote-authority.test.ts:894 pins only resolvedBy containing "superseded", not resolution.

Two sub-claims in the finding are overstated. (1) The audit timeline does not record a denial on this path: the catch emits no authorization.denied event and no memory.record; the only event is mission.permission_required from the re-ask. The "deny" value is visible only in the stored request record and in the raw projection at src/lib/bunny-host/presentation.ts:551-553, which spreads full request objects into mission.requests. (2) presentation.ts:359-374 shows "Denied" only when step.state is "failed" and resolution is "deny", and the step is in waiting_for_approval with the new pendingRequestId, so the UI label is not triggered here. A consumer reading the raw requests array would still see resolution "deny" on the superseded entry, which contradicts the code comment.

Not an owner-policy disposition or listed accepted limitation. Not refuted, since the stored record is wrong, but impact is LOW and cosmetic with respect to authority. I did not run the single test or any probes; the conclusions come from reading the code paths listed above.

The finding is real, but its stated mechanism is partly wrong. Verified by code reading only; no probe run and no repo files touched.

Confirmed:
- pendingRemoteReview() (manager.server.ts:2316-2327) is Host-wide. store.server.ts:158 pendingRemoteChanges() has no mission filter. The listing is built from describeRemoteChange (sha256 prefix, size, 600-char preview).
- bus.server.ts:171 puts that listing into the ask reason for any code-running or git.* ask on any Mission, and that reason is stored on the request.
- Device GET /state is NOT the leak path. http.server.ts:369 runs dashboardSnapshot(deviceSnapshot(...)) for devices. presentation.ts:~552 replaces every request.reason with a generic "Authorize X in this mission's approved workspace..." string. The finding's claim that viewFor carries the listing to devices is therefore wrong.
- The leak is through mission.get. commands.server.ts:80 returns deviceMissionData(view) for devices. manager.server.ts:2229 strips only desktopGrant/desktopOperation/desktopBinding and keeps reason. view() (manager.server.ts:493-527) returns requests with the stored reason, and get() (manager.server.ts:529) passes them through. http.server.ts:506 authorises mission.get for devices as a read, with no mission scoping. A device can therefore read the listing from any Mission's pending code-running request.

Impact is limited:
- The previews cover only unacknowledged paths in remote_changes. Those are files written under remote-authority envelopes, so they are normally device-authored content, not workstation secrets.
- Devices already see all Missions (deviceSnapshot does not filter missions), and mission.get already exposes events and memory cross-mission. This is an incremental disclosure, not a new class of access.
- Nothing here authorises execution or any action. Owner-policy dispositions and accepted limitations do not cover it, so it is not refuted.

Recommended fix: have deviceMissionData (manager.server.ts:2229) replace or strip the review listing in request.reason, or drop the content preview for device views.

Not refuted. The disclosure is real, but the finding picks the wrong channel and understates it. Code path, all verified by reading (no probe run; repo untouched; no test-results change):

1. The listing does reach a device. bus.server.ts:171 puts review.listing (size, SHA-256 prefix, 600-char preview) into the ask reason. It is also copied into the event log: bus.server.ts:259 emits "authorization.required" with decision.reason. A device's mission.get returns events.slice(-200) unfiltered (manager.server.ts:533).

2. The bigger channel is pre-existing and not reviewed by the finding. For a device, commands.server.ts:80 returns missions.get(id) with no per-device filter. manager.server.ts:529-539 returns mission events (last 200), memory (last 60), and runs (last 50) with full params. deviceMissionData (manager.server.ts:2228-2230) strips only desktopGrant/desktopOperation/desktopBinding from requests. http.server.ts:767-777 projects only extra.agents, extra.agent and extra.mission, so extra.data passes through via ...extra. Each run record stores the full params (bus.server.ts:261-263 and store.server.ts:245-247), so a filesystem.write run carries its complete content, and terminal.exec runs carry their args. The same is true for workstation Missions, not just remote-written ones. At 7fbea39 manager.server.ts:481 already had runs with params and commands.server.ts:78 returned missions.get unfiltered, so this predates the diff. The device still cannot execute anything from it.

3. Consequence: the recommended fix (strip the listing from reason) would not close the leak. A device can already read full file content of any Mission's writes via mission.get runs, and the listing text via events. The proper fix is a device projection of mission.get that redacts runs params, events and memory outside what the device is allowed to see.

Severity: the listing alone is LOW (confidentiality only, bounded to 600 characters). The same device-visible mission.get path exposes full run params for every Mission, including workstation-run file contents and command arguments, so MEDIUM is the honest rating. It is not execution, and devices are permitted to view Mission state, so it is not BLOCKER or HIGH. None of the owner dispositions or accepted limitations covers this.

The classifier fact is accurate: probe in a temp dir (node --experimental-strip-types importing authorization.server.ts by file URL) returned runsCode=false and remoteExecutionRefusal=null for github.pr_list, github.issue_list and github.repo_view, while git.status and git.diff also return runsCode=false and null. The bus gate at bus.server.ts:169 and live-code tracking at bus.server.ts:308 test only runsCode(...) || action.startsWith("git."), so github.* runs without the Host-wide review. The review gate's own stated scope (round 7/8 text) is terminal, Git mutations and reads, non-Calculator EXECUTE and shell-capable provider sessions; gh is not in that list. The finding's security impact does not hold. The review gate exists because Git reads can run owner-configured textconv, clean or fsmonitor programs over working-tree files. gh's read queries (pr list, issue list, repo view) do not read working-tree content, and the spawn is shell-free (process.server.ts:69, shell:false) with Git children hardened under remote authority (connectors.server.ts:46 sets GIT_CONFIG_* for fsmonitor, hooksPath and diff.external). The config files gh's Git children could read are protected from device writes: .git segments (GIT_SEGMENT), .gitattributes, .gitmodules, .gitconfig and all executables or scripts are refused by remoteExecutionRefusal, which admits only inert data extensions outside execution-config paths. So a paired device cannot make github.* run any program or file it wrote. Residual point: github.* is absent from runsCode, so it is inconsistent with the Git-read rationale. Treat it as defense-in-depth consistency at most. I did not run gh against a live remote; the no-execution conclusion rests on the config-file protections above. No repo files were modified and no repo tests were run, so test-results/ is untouched.

The finding is confirmed as a coverage gap, but no concrete device-triggered code execution was found, so I keep it at LOW and do not refute it.

Verified in source:
- authorization.server.ts:238-240: runsCode() returns true only for terminal.exec, GIT_MUTATIONS, and non-Calculator EXECUTE. The github.* READ actions fall through to false.
- authorization.server.ts:119-124 and 173-175: GIT_MUTATIONS does not include github.*, and remoteCalculatorOperation does not apply to them.
- authorization.server.ts:217-236: remoteExecutionRefusal() returns null for github.pr_list, github.issue_list and github.repo_view, so a remote envelope with network allowed runs them without a desktop step (decide() at 332 allows them once network.allowed is true).
- bus.server.ts:169: the review gate tests runsCode(...) || action.startsWith("git.") only, so github.* skips the Host-wide review gate.
- bus.server.ts:308: the liveCode set (and so the mid-run hold) uses the same test, so in-flight gh reads are not counted as live code.
- connectors.server.ts:44-46: under remote authority gh gets GIT_CONFIG hardening (fsmonitor off, hooksPath redirected, diff.external blank, pager cat) and runs owned: true.

Probe (temp folder under the OS temp dir, deleted afterwards, no repo files touched): runsCode for github.pr_list, github.issue_list and github.repo_view returns false, runsCode for git.status also returns false (the bus gate covers git.* separately), and remoteExecutionRefusal for github.pr_list and github.repo_view returns null.

Why it is not a BLOCKER or HIGH: gh does not run project files, and the planted-program routes are closed. The device cannot write .git/* config, .gitattributes or any executable, because executionConfigPath blocks .git segments and .gitattributes, and inertDataPath blocks .exe, .cmd and .bat. Windows CreateProcess and libuv search for "gh" only try gh.com and gh.exe, so a device-written data file cannot shadow it. Read-only gh calls do not invoke hooks, filters or extensions, and gh's git children get the same hardening as Bunny's own git reads. The only remaining exposure is the owner-configured global filter/config limitation already listed as accepted.

It still breaks the stated invariant "no non-direct Bunny program run starts while a paired-device change is unacknowledged", which lists git reads explicitly. The bus comment at bus.server.ts:168 gives the same reason for covering git reads, and that reason applies to gh. The recommended fix (treat connector actions that spawn a program as code-running for the review gate and liveCode) is reasonable. Repo test-results/ were not touched, since no repo test was run.

Confirmed by a probe. Copied src/lib/bunny-missions/remote-authority.test.ts into a mkdtemp folder under the OS temp dir, rewrote its relative imports to absolute file URLs, and appended one test. The test used the existing setup/phoneApprove/waitAsk helpers. A paired device wrote notes.txt (763 bytes) through filesystem.write: 690 bytes of "// ..." comment filler, then a line `require('fs').writeFileSync('ran.flag','x') // payload-ran`. A workstation Mission then ran terminal.exec node notes.txt. The ask reason was: "Approval required on Windows Host: this runs code over files changed under paired-device authority. Review their content before allowing: • ...notes.txt: 763 bytes, sha256 0416841dbbd9ffc8…, content: \"// benign header line ⏎ ... ⏎ // ben…\"". The string "payload-ran" was not visible in the prompt, and ran.flag did not exist before approval. After respond(ask.id, "allow_once", "workstation") the mission state was "completed" and ran.flag was created. The cause is in the code: manager.server.ts describeRemoteChange (~line 80) shows only bytes.subarray(0,600) of the file, pendingRemoteReview (~2316-2326) lists only that preview, and the allow_once path (~3646-3648) acknowledges the remote_changes record IDs, not the bytes or the hash the prompt showed. Nothing else in the path binds the executed bytes to the shown hash. The "…" truncation marker is visible, which is a partial mitigation, and a human workstation click is still required, so this is human-mediated rather than a pure device-only execution. It still defeats the authoritative review gate that the owner described ("workstation reviews content before code runs"), so I keep HIGH. Not an owner-listed disposition or accepted limitation. Coverage: the repo test suite was not run. The repo was not edited. Only the probe's own temp folder was used. That folder (C:\Users\allam\AppData\Local\Temp\r9a-btvRvq) could not be deleted because bash tool shells still held it, so it is a leftover in OS temp outside the repo.

Not refuted. The truncation and the sanitizer gap are real, but the impact is an approver-assurance limitation, not a device-caused execution path, so LOW.

Verified in code (src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts):
- Lines 74-84 describeRemoteChange: reads the whole file (readFileSync at line 78), hashes it, then shows only bytes.subarray(0, 600) (line 80) plus "…" when size > 600. The tail is never shown.
- Line 80 sanitizer char class covers ‪-‮ and ⁦-⁩ but not U+200E/U+200F. Probe in a temp dir (since deleted): a 596-character preview kept both U+200E and U+200F, and a payload placed after byte 600 was not shown. So the bidi gap is real, though LRM/RLM only affect neutral-character ordering and are a weak spoofing vector.
- Line 2324 calls describeRemoteChange for up to REVIEW_PAGE=12 paths on each pendingRemoteReview() call. pendingRemoteReview is reached from missionScopeCheck (line 119), bus.remoteReviewFor (line 172), line 1446, and respond (line 3633). Write size is capped at 1 MiB (local.server.ts:12, 107), so each gate evaluation can synchronously read and hash up to about 12 MiB. This is an availability cost; the review-hold it causes is fail-closed.
- Mitigations already present: mintDesktopGrant (manager.server.ts ~2370-2376) binds mutationSequence, so any change after the ask forces a re-ask. respond acknowledges only the shown ids. The device itself never runs code; execution still requires a workstation allow_once on a desktop-required ask.

Why it is not refuted: the owner's spec does list a 600-character preview, but the spec does not say an approver may approve code execution over content they could not see. No listed disposition covers that case. The finding is a legitimate, reproducible limitation with a fail-closed-adjacent impact, so it stays at LOW.

Repo files were not modified. The remote-authority test was not run. No test-results/ changes.

Refuted as a security or correctness defect; the residual sanitizer gap is INFO. Evidence was source reading only (no probes, no repo edits, no test runs, so test-results/ is untouched).

Facts confirmed:
- manager.server.ts:74-86 truncates the preview to bytes.subarray(0,600), shows size and a 16-hex SHA prefix, and reads the whole file synchronously with readFileSync.
- The sanitizer regex at line 80 omits U+200E and U+200F (LRM/RLM). The rest of the bidi controls (202a-202e, 2066-2069) are covered.
- Device writes are capped at 1 MiB (capabilities/local.server.ts:107), so the full read is bounded at about 12 MiB hashed per gate call, not unbounded.

Why it does not hold as a device-caused execution or envelope-escape issue:
- The 600-character bounded preview with size and SHA is the owner's stated design in the review brief. The finding itself calls the truncation "a truncation limit of the stated design".
- A device cannot cause code execution by truncation. The workstation must still give an allow_once, and the ack is bound to the exact remote_changes row ids shown at ask time (manager.server.ts:3647, store.server.ts:161). Each write records a fresh random UUID row (store.server.ts:155, bus.server.ts:307), so any change after the ask stays unacknowledged and the gate re-asks.
- The recording at bus.server.ts:307 happens synchronously before adapter.execute at line 322, with no await in between for the filesystem.write branch, so there is no interleaving window where a listed row could be acknowledged over content that changed later.
- The read-cost point is availability only and bounded by the 1 MiB write cap.

The gap is real in the code, so I did not refute it. Tracing the path:

Impact is limited. Confirmed by reading the code (no files changed, no probe re-run):
- commands.server.ts:50-61: mission.start is in REMOTE, so a device may call it. For non-local access it only runs deviceStartRefusal (line 60).
- manager.server.ts:2177-2211 (deviceStartRefusal): a workstation envelope (isRemoteEnvelope false, line 2180) is refused only if it has shell sessions, terminal, or commit/merge/worktree git actions, or if a non-completed step has an exec-class operation the workstation envelope would run unasked. A pure filesystem.write plan passes, so a device can start it.
- manager.server.ts:856-867 (MissionManager.start): records no actor. Mission.origin is set at create (commands.server.ts:23-29), and devices cannot create Missions (mission.create is not in REMOTE), so origin does not reveal a device start.
- manager.server.ts:2303-2311 (remoteActorFor): returns null for a workstation envelope unless the step's approvedOnce was answered by a device. A device-started, never-asked write has no approvedOnce, so the actor is null.
- manager.server.ts:2340-2350 (remoteMutationHeld) returns null with no actor, and manager.server.ts:173-180 (remoteMutationStarted) records nothing. So neither the mid-run hold nor the review ledger sees the write. bus.server.ts:165 and :307 match this.

Why it is LOW, not MEDIUM:
- The device cannot choose content. The write params come from the workstation-approved plan (replan, plan, and create-with-steps are workstation-only; mission.replan is not in REMOTE). The device controls only timing.
- No device-authored code runs. Starting a pure-write Mission is what the owner-approved deviceStartRefusal design allows, and planned in-envelope writes are an explicitly permitted device operation.
- The consequence is that workstation-approved, plan-fixed content can land under live workstation code without the hold, and that later workstation prompts would not list the write in remoteChanges(). That breaks the round-4 mid-run-hold invariant, which is a real correctness gap, but it is not a device-driven code execution or an action outside the reviewed envelope.

The recommended fix (record the starting actor on the Mission and treat device-started mutations as device-attributable, or refuse device start while liveCodeExecutions() is non-empty) is reasonable.

Not refuted. I re-read the code paths and found no guard that stops the described case. I did not run a probe and did not run any test, so the repo is untouched.

Confirmed mechanics:
- manager.server.ts:2340-2347 (remoteMutationHeld): when request.stepId is set and step.approvedOnce.action === request.action and the answering actor is 'workstation' (isTrustedLocalActor = actor === "workstation", authorization.server.ts:176), it returns null before the liveCodeExecutions() check. Params, path and digest are never compared.
- manager.server.ts:2303-2312 (remoteActorFor): a remote envelope always yields its device as the actor, so a device-attributable write on a remote Mission step is covered by the hold check.
- skills.server.ts:80 and the step loop: skill sub-requests spread ...request, so they carry stepId and oneTimeAction. Each skill write is therefore a separate bus request on the same step.
- bus.server.ts:175: oneTime = oneTimeAction === action, and authorization.server.ts:374 returns allow for oneTime before scopeViolation runs. Within a skill, every later filesystem.write on that step is admitted without a per-path check. The adapter's roots remain envelope.projectRoots. This is the existing skill one-time design.
- approvedOnce persists until the step completes, is retried, or the Host restarts (manager.server.ts:3917, 4161, 4222), so a multi-write skill step keeps the exemption for its whole run.
- bus.server.ts:308 and 349: liveCode is Host-wide and set for any runsCode request, including a long-running workstation-approved command or a direct run. Steps within one Mission run concurrently (manager.server.ts tickOnce, maxConcurrentAgents). So the exemption is reachable when a workstation-approved long-running process is in flight while a device skill step holds a workstation one-time filesystem.write approval.

Why LOW: the exposure needs a multi-write skill step, a workstation one-time answer on that step, and concurrent live code. The writes are limited to the data types allowed by remoteExecutionRefusal and to envelope roots. Subsequent code runs still wait on the Host-wide review gate. The impact is that device-chosen data can reach already-approved live code during its run, which is the case the mid-run hold is meant to cover. It is not a direct path to launching a new executable. The reviewer's recommendation (bind the exemption to the exact operation, or consume the one-time allowance on first use) is sound.
